tweet_summary: Claims as an 'UPDATE' that Ohio nurse Chanda Petrey-Czaruk — who posted a video wishing harm on Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt during childbirth — 'has been taken into custody! FAFO!'
why_note_decision: The tweet's headline claim — that the nurse 'has been taken into custody' — is false. Reporting confirms she lost her job (former VP of First Choice Home Health; no longer employed) and faced public backlash, but there is no indication she was arrested or detained; wishing harm in a video is generally protected speech, not a crime. Even a top reply notes she was NOT arrested. Asserting a fabricated arrest about a named private individual to ~800k viewers is exactly the kind of false, checkable claim a note should correct.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note clearly states she was NOT taken into custody / arrested (no arrest occurred). It may add the accurate context that she lost her job / is a former employee of First Choice Home Health, but the indispensable correction is the false arrest claim. Must cite reliable reporting. FAIL if the note affirms or implies she was arrested/detained, or only quibbles about employment details while leaving the false 'taken into custody' claim unaddressed (that would be PARTIAL/insufficient).
reference_note: The nurse Chanda Petrey-Czaruk is a former employee of First Choice Home Health and was not taken into custody. https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us/us-news/chanda-petrey-czaruk-ohio-nurse-former-firstchoice-vice-president-viral-video-karoline-leavitt-pregnant-article-153480431 https://sundayguardianlive.com/world/who-is-chanda-petrey-czaruk-ohio-nurse-at-center-of-viral-controversy-after-wishing-injury-on-white-house-press-secretary-and-facing-backlash-165620

fact_check.notes: She posted a video wishing a traumatic childbirth injury on Karoline Leavitt; lost her job (former VP, First Choice Home Health; no longer employed at Baptist Health). No source reports any arrest or custody. The tweet's 'taken into custody' claim is fabricated. A reply (@unhealthytruth) also says she was not arrested.

importance.lens_rationale: 800k impressions on a fabricated-arrest claim about a named individual, feeding a harassment pile-on; correcting false 'they got arrested' rage-bait protects against mob misinformation and reputational harm.
